Justice, and may it please the Court:
 Pleading an affirmative defense is
 ordinarily a precondition for invoking that
 defense to bar or limit a claim.  Kontrick held
that ordinarily, under the civil rules, a
defense is lost if it's not included in an
 amended plain -- complaint -- in an amended
 defense or in the original defense.  There's no
reason to depart in this case from those
 established rules.
 The Eleventh Circuit's Hassan decision
improperly permits a defendant to invoke an
 affirmative defense which it has never pled.
 It has several fatal flaws.
 First, it effectively rewrites Rules 8
